title: Oven Rack Placement, Preheating, and Convection: Techniques from Techniquely with Lan Lam
summary: America’s Test Kitchen’s Techniquely episode with Lan Lam explains common oven mistakes and how to fix them by focusing on rack placement, full preheating, and heat sources. The video demonstrates practical setups for thin-crust pizza on a stone with the rack close to the broiler, a bottom-rack strategy for cast-iron pan pizzas, and broiled zucchini, then discusses convection’s effects on multiple racks, browning, and timing, culminating in three core takeaways: adjust the rack, let the oven fully heat, and tailor convection with notes for future tweaks.
topics: bottom rack for cast-iron pan pizza
electric vs dual-fuel oven heating cycles

sections.title: Oven Basics: Preheating, Rack Position, and Temperature Calibration
sections.description: Intro on why waiting for full preheat, proper rack placement, and calibrated temperatures matter for recipe success; mentions using an oven thermometer and awareness of typical temperature drift.

sections.title: Pizza Rack Placement and Bake Setup
sections.description: Demonstrates how rack position relative to the broiler and the use of a pizza stone influence browning and bake speed for thin-crust pizza.

sections.title: Preheat Demonstration and Oven Heat Cycles
sections.description: Illustrates the difference between a fully heated oven and the ongoing cycle as the oven reaches and maintains target temperature, including how dual-element ovens behave.

sections.title: Bottom Rack for Cast-Iron Pan Pizza and Heat Distribution
sections.description: Explains why placing the rack at the bottom uses oven-floor heat to help dough rise and cook while keeping cheese from burning before the crust is ready.

sections.title: Broiler Basics and Zucchini Technique
sections.description: Discusses how proximity to the broiler concentrates heat and how distance changes heat distribution; shows a zucchini technique to create varied textures and browning.

sections.title: Convection Baking: Benefits, Limits, and Adjustments
sections.description: Outlines what convection does for browning and speed, with caveats about differences across recipes and guidance to reduce temperature by about 25°F and track results for future adjustments.

sections.title: Three Key Takeaways
sections.description: Concise recap of essential practices for reliable oven results: adjust the rack and center food, wait for full preheat, and adjust convection use with documentation.

featured_techniques.technique: Verify oven temperature with an oven thermometer
Position oven rack 4–5 inches from the broiler for thin crust pizza
Place pizza stone on rack and bake at 500°F
Use bottom rack for cast-iron pan pizza to utilize oven-floor heat
Understand full heat cycle: top element off, bottom cycles to maintain temp
Completely preheat before adding food for even cooking
Broiler heat is very intense up close; distance affects heat distribution
Smash zucchini into large uneven pieces for varied textures
Set rack closer to the broiler to encourage charring on some pieces
Convection: reduce temperature by 25°F when using convection
Keep notes on temperatures, times, and results to reproduce results
Three essential oven practices: rack adjustment, full heat, convection adjustments
